channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Nederland (businessinsider.nl)

item.title: My 8-step plan for Dario Amodei to get off the Pentagon's naughty list
item.description: Pentagon blacklists Anthropic, citing supply chain risks. Other tech leaders have shown the way to work with the Trump administration.

item.title: I inherited a storage unit from a family friend. It was full of vintage clothes, which I now sell online.
item.description: A friend's grandfather boxed up his sporting goods store in 1990. Decades later, we found the untouched inventory.

item.title: I'm polyamorous and my 2 partners and I live with our kids. Here's how we navigate coparenting together.
item.description: I know our life isn't typical, but it works well for our family. I'm happy that our kids have three parents who care for them.

item.title: Travelers are waiting hours at airport security as unpaid TSA agents stop showing up for work
item.description: Many TSA agents, who are not getting paid due to the partial government shutdown, have stopped working. That means long waits at airport security.

item.title: Oil passes $100 a barrel as US energy secretary says Iran won't be a 'long-term war'
item.description: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright blamed "emotional reactions" for the surge in gas prices and said they should return to normal in weeks, not months.

item.title: I'm a 78-year-old retiree who's vibe coding. Being out of the workforce doesn't mean we can't use AI like tech pros.
item.description: At 78, he's vibe coding and teaching AI to seniors. Retirement hasn't slowed his passion for technology.

item.title: I took a $185 lie-flat overnight bus across Europe instead of the train. It was slower — but I slept better.
item.description: On board the bus from Amsterdam to Zurich, the hotel-grade bathroom was roomy, well lit, and plush enough for a nighttime routine.

item.title: The CEO of a $15 billion AI company says the biggest AI winners won't be software — they'll be mines, farms, and trucks
item.description: The CEO of a $15 billion AI company says the biggest AI winners won't be software but industries like farming, mining, and trucking.

item.title: Coach's former CEO said Gen Z is most similar to the 60s generation
item.description: Lew Frankfort, who grew up in the sixties, said Gen Z has similar ideas on value and authenticity.

item.title: I'm 73, still working, and walk 20,000 steps a day. I can do the splits — and I'm not slowing down.
item.description: Victor Chan, a former bodybuilder, says he stretches every day and makes a point to talk to his younger neighbors.
